clue.text: Speech at end of month to present gong?

indicators.note: the speech is placed at the end of the month, so it comes after it in the answer

parts.note: Dec is the standard abbreviation for December
an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: Someone gives an address at the close of the month before handing out a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gong' is British slang for a medal or honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A gong is informal British slang for a medal, and a medal awarded for service is called a decoration.

clue.text: Depicted as tense

definitions.meaning: something sketched or pictured with a pencil
strained and anxious-looking, as a haggard face is

explanation.surface: A picture shown as stressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawn is the past participle of draw (to sketch), and it also describes a face looking strained and tired.

clue.text: Chelsea erred — unruly supporters egging others on

indicators.note: unruly letters are disorderly, so the fodder's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Chelsea football fans got out of hand while urging on the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: Chelsea is a London football club, which makes 'unruly supporters' read as football hooligans.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerleaders are people who lead the crowd's chanting, urging others to back a team.

clue.text: Bird in stream hiding head

indicators.note: the stream's word conceals its first letter, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a brook is a small stream

explanation.surface: A bird ducks its head under the water of a brook.
explanation.definitionFit: The rook is a black crow-family bird of farmland.

clue.text: Article on French department reveals everything

indicators.note: in a down clue the article sits on top of the department, so it comes first

parts.note: the definite article
the Lot is a department of south-west France

explanation.surface: A news piece on a region of France tells all.
explanation.definitionFit: 'The lot' is an informal idiom meaning all of it, the whole amount.

clue.text: Honoured officer is bearing down on worker toeing the line

indicators.note: in a down clue the first pieces press down on top of the worker, so they come before it

parts.note: an OBE is an Officer of the Order of the British Empire, a UK honour
taken as written
a worker ant, the usual crossword worker

explanation.surface: A decorated officer leans hard on an employee who is obeying orders.
explanation.walkthrough: OBE (Officer of the Order of the British Empire) is a British honour, hence 'Honoured officer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeisant means deferential and obedient, behaving with submissive respect, just like someone conforming to rules.

clue.text: Administrator, an ordinary person keeping grip on island one way and another

indicators.note: the ordinary person holds the island letters within their grasp

parts.note: a commoner is someone without noble rank

indicators.note: the island abbreviation is written once forwards and then again the other way round

explanation.surface: An official is a regular person who clutches an island from every side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one way and another' means the island is written forwards and then backwards, making ISSI; 'keeping grip on' has the ordinary person holding that run.
explanation.definitionFit: A commissioner is an official put in charge of a department, a body or a region, so an administrator.

clue.text: Drink with gritty stuff, hard to get swallowed

indicators.note: the hard letter is taken down inside the gritty word

parts.note: sandy describes something full of grit
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A beverage with grit in it that is tough to get down.
explanation.walkthrough: A shandy is a British drink of beer mixed with lemonade.
explanation.definitionFit: A shandy is a beverage of beer diluted with lemonade or ginger beer.

clue.text: Unusual name given to one flowering plant

indicators.note: an unusual arrangement of the letters, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An odd title given to a single blooming plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The anemone, or windflower, is a buttercup-family plant grown for its showy blooms.

clue.text: Period of aspiration suffering setback, Conservative admitted

explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering setback' reverses HOPE to EPOH, and 'admitted' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a distinct era of history, a long span of time.

clue.text: Socially inept fellow participating in dinner-dance

indicators.note: the answer takes part within the words, its letters lying inside them

explanation.surface: An awkward man joins in at a dinner-dance.

clue.text: Medical student trained to be so humane

indicators.note: the letters are trained into a new arrangement, an anagram

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a houseman is a newly qualified junior doctor in a hospital post, so 'Medical student' is a loose fit.
explanation.definitionFit: A houseman is a junior hospital doctor still in training, close to a medical student.

clue.text: One of an older generation having son react badly

indicators.note: the letters are put together badly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grandparent whose boy responds poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancestor is a forebear from earlier in a family line, such as a great-grandparent.

clue.text: Good person, a German author

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good person
ein is the German word for a

explanation.surface: A kind German writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Gertrude Stein was an American writer; 'a German' is the word ein, not the author's nationality.

clue.text: Cruel person being unhappy is repentant ultimately

parts.note: sad means unhappy
taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

clue.text: A street in New York is unpleasant

clue.text: You and I to descend on mostly pebbly seaside resort

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece comes down on top of the rest, so it is placed first

parts.note: we is the pronoun for you and I together

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: stony means full of pebbles

explanation.surface: We arrive at a shingle beach town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims STONY to STON. Weston-super-Mare is an English seaside town on the Bristol Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: Weston-super-Mare, often shortened, is a traditional English coastal holiday town.

clue.text: Comedian with repeated hesitation, one stumbling around?

indicators.note: the hesitation sound is given twice

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A comic stammers again and again, maybe tripping about.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Dodd was a long-running British stand-up comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodderer is a shaky, unsteady person, often elderly, who totters about.

clue.text: Man on board trying to avoid a mate

definitions.text: Man on board trying to avoid a mate

parts.words: Man on board trying to avoid a mate
parts.note: a man is a chess piece, and checkmate falls on this one piece, which must escape it

explanation.definitionFit: In chess the game is lost when this royal piece is checkmated, so it must always evade mate.
